agentCan: Implement the full OAuth V2 handler, token storage, and reinstall/scope-change messaging
Maintain the scope list and draft scope justifications for review
Generate the install URL and Add-to-Slack button markup
Draft the review submission packet (test accounts, demo video script)

approval.trigger: No approval needed for OAuth itself. The Slack Marketplace review is OPTIONAL and only for directory listing: requires 10+ active (past-28-day) workspaces before you can even submit; preliminary review up to 10 business days + functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions (both stated). Preliminary queue place resets on every resubmission.
approval.wait: None for OAuth; up to ~12 weeks worst-case for a Marketplace listing

blockers.detail: You cannot submit for Marketplace review until the app is installed on 10+ active workspaces (used in the past 28 days, not sandboxes). For a new agent product this adds real calendar time before listing.
blockers.howToClear: Ship via your Sharable URL / Add-to-Slack button first; treat the listing as phase two.
blockers.title: 10-active-workspace gate before listing review

blockers.detail: Using Slack data to train LLMs is explicitly prohibited by the App Developer Policy. Apps whose only functionality is an MCP server (no meaningful in-Slack functionality) are listed as unsuitable.
blockers.howToClear: Design genuine in-Slack functionality; never train on workspace data.
blockers.title: LLM-training ban and MCP-only rejection

blockers.detail: After publishing, the live app config is locked: scope or redirect-URL changes need resubmission and approval, and users must reinstall.
blockers.howToClear: Finalize scopes before submitting; message users in-app about reinstalls when scopes change.
blockers.title: Post-publish config lock

alternatives: Sign in with Slack (separate identity/login feature; cannot be mixed with install scopes in one flow)
flavor.recommended: Modern granular-permissions Slack app, OAuth V2
flavor.why: The current standard. Use bot token scopes as the app's identity and user token scopes only when acting on behalf of a specific user. Granular scopes map cleanly to least-privilege agent design and to review expectations.

humanMust: Create the app and click through the config portal under your own Slack account
Enter redirect URLs and select scopes (no official programmatic app-creation API found)
Provide test account credentials and a demo video for any Marketplace submission
name: Slack
nuances: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS, cannot contain anchors, and the same redirect_uri must be sent in both the authorize and token-exchange steps or you get a bad_redirect_uri error. Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes.
Request minimum scopes and be able to demonstrate every one: reviewers check that each scope is used, and ungranted optional scopes must be handled gracefully.
Workspaces with Admin-Approved Apps can block installs; org-level (admin.*) scopes need an Org Admin/Owner install.
Broken privacy-policy/support links or substantially changed functionality without resubmission can get a listed app delisted.
prerequisites: A Slack account and a development workspace
The minimal bot (and optionally user) scopes your agent needs

steps.detail: Sign in, open api.slack.com/apps, click Create an App > From scratch, name the app, pick your development workspace, Create App.
steps.title: Create the Slack app

steps.detail: Basic Information > App Credentials: copy the Client ID and Client Secret (plus Signing Secret if you will verify events).
steps.title: Copy app credentials

steps.detail: OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs: add your OAuth callback URL (HTTPS, no anchors) and Save URLs. Then add scopes under Bot Token Scopes (and User Token Scopes only if you act as the user). Keep scopes minimal and justifiable.
steps.title: Register redirect URLs and scopes

steps.detail: Install the app to your dev workspace to get tokens flowing for development.
steps.title: Install to your dev workspace

steps.detail: Send users to slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with scope, user_scope, client_id, redirect_uri, state; handle the redirect; exchange the code at slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access (code expires in 10 minutes). Store the xoxb- bot token (and xoxp- user token, if any) server-side.
steps.title: Implement the OAuth V2 handler

steps.detail: In app settings: Manage Distribution > get the green check on all four sections under 'Share Your App with Other Workspaces' > Activate Public Distribution. Any workspace can now install via your Sharable URL / Add-to-Slack button. No approval, no wait.
steps.title: Activate public distribution

steps.detail: (Optional, for directory listing) First reach 10+ active workspaces. Then submit from the app's config page: automated tests run, then a two-stage manual review (preliminary up to 10 business days, functional up to 10 weeks for new submissions). Provide test credentials and a demo video of install > OAuth > setup > end-to-end use > uninstall.
steps.time: Packet prep ~1 day; waiting up to ~12 weeks
steps.title: (Optional) Submit to the Slack Marketplace

tagline: OAuth works the day you flip on public distribution, no approval. The Marketplace listing is optional but gated: 10+ active workspaces before you can even submit, and up to ~12 weeks of review.

time.active: ~1 hour of portal config + normal OAuth backend work
time.total: Same day to working OAuth; up to ~12 weeks if you pursue a Marketplace listing
time.waiting: None for OAuth; stated review windows for listing only
